Triage: lands in `domain:spec` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, TSDoc only); rationale below — ⚠️ **and I nearly closed this, so the reasoning is worth stating rather than asserting.**

**Why the obvious reading says close.** The threshold's (a) boundary, landed this morning in PR #16557, is 「(a) 的分界是不完整 vs 错误…漏列成员不是」. The card's own words are *"literally true and structurally incomplete."* On that reading it closes, and the harm direction even errs safe — a reader who believes the switch does **less** than it does is over-cautious, not under-.

**Why it does not close: PR #16196 merged, and that changed the sentence's status.** Before that PR, this was one partial sentence among partial siblings. That PR corrected the **same fact in three places** — the `publicSharing.enabled` property comment ~30 lines below, `IShareLinkService.resolveToken`'s `null`-cause list, and design note 7 — and left this one. ⇒ It is no longer *incomplete*; it is the **contradicted half of a fact the same file now states correctly 30 lines away**, and a reader has no signal telling them which of the two is current. That is not an omitted member. `Bug`.

⭐ **Boundary refinement worth recording, because this is its third instance today**: *a true-but-partial statement becomes admissible once its complement has landed elsewhere and it was not updated* — one fact, N carriers, N−1 corrected. The same shape graded in today's round as #16289 (driver-sql: three sites use `formatDuplicateGroups`, the fourth hand-rolls it, and the drift is already real) and #16477 (five comments naming a file renamed everywhere else). ⛔ The trigger is the landed correction, not the partiality — before #16196 this really was out of class.

`priority:p3`, matching #14703's own grade as the card proposes: no consumer is wrong, no gate is red, no authoring surface moves. ⛔ Do not let "security-relevant" pull it up — the switch works correctly; only its description is stale.

⭐ **The card's disagreement with the dev was the right call and the containment argument is genuinely wrong.** A reader asking *"what does `enabled: false` do?"* meets a self-contained, authoritative-sounding sentence at block level with **no signal that it is partial** — so nothing sends them down to the property comment. The block doc is also the more likely landing site: it is what a reader scanning the object schema for the sharing policy hits first, and it carries the `@see` pointers that make it read as orientation text for the whole block. ⇒ #14703 corrected the property; the sentence most likely to be read still says the old thing, which partially defeats that fix.

⛔ **This is not a criticism of #16196 or its dev, and the grade must not be read as one.** That card was ruled to exactly two sites, the dev respected the fence, **declared this observation as a deviation rather than burying it**, and recorded it in the PR's "Out of scope, noted for the PM". ⭐ That declaration is the only reason this is answerable at all — it is the behaviour the fence is supposed to produce.

**Scope — ⛔ deliberately one clause, and the fences are load-bearing:**
- ⛔ **Do not restate the standing-policy explanation here.** #16196 put the mechanism on `enabled` and in design note 7; a second full copy is exactly the drift this family keeps generating. ⇒ A pointer plus the missing clause is the whole job — e.g. *"…refuses to create share-link rows for this object, **and refuses to resolve any that already exist** (#14033 — see `enabled` below)"*.
- ⛔ **Do not touch the `.describe()` string** — it feeds `content/docs/references/**` and forces `gen:schema && gen:docs`. Same fence #14703 and #16196 both carried; #16196's verification proves it holds (`check:docs`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface` green after rebuild, 0 generated files in the diff).
- ⛔ #15239 (`sharing.zod.ts` docblocks) is a different file — ⛔ do not fold in.

Clause-② no, per the card. ⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

- Disjoint from everything this seat has in flight: `functional-completeness.{ts,test.ts}` + `rest-hook-script-fault-envelope.test.ts` (#16441, PR #16956, awaiting green); `contracts/automation-service.ts` + `ui/app.zod.ts` + one `examples/app-multi-package` file (#16708 + #16507, PR #16958, awaiting green); `ui/dashboard.zod.ts` (#16256, same wave); `lint/validate-security-posture.ts` + five `cli/test/serve-*.e2e.test.ts` (#16517, same wave).
- H17 hold trigger-file index on patrol anchor #9857: **zero rows** for `object.zod.ts`.

Gate ① fails against both — #16256 is a `.describe()` string plus a docs regeneration, #16517 is a provenance table split plus five test fixtures; three different defect shapes and three different fix methods. Parallel is legal because the surfaces above are disjoint.

## ACCEPT — PR #16964, reviewed in seat at 2026-09-08T20:23Z

`domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_016N6xmWt5hYm94ffVEwGH8x`. Review run against `origin/main` `97adce2fa`. ⛔ Every reading below is this seat's own; the dev's report was the prompt to check, not the evidence.

### ① Premises, re-measured independently

`publicSharing: strictObject({` at `object.zod.ts:2250`; the stale sentence `refuses to create share-link rows` occurs **exactly once** in that file. Both hold.

### ⭐ The runtime claim, checked rather than accepted

The card's whole argument is that the switch is a **standing policy**, not a mint-time check. The report asserted it; this seat read the plugin. `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts` on `origin/main`:

```
:459   if (!policy.enabled && !this.permissive && !context.isSystem) {     ← createLink — HAS the bypass
:707   if (!policy.enabled) {                                             ← redemption — policy.enabled ALONE
:683   // `permissive` bypass (system-context ledger row 37) carries no mark of …
```

⇒ **The mint path has a bypass and the redemption path does not.** That is precisely the asymmetry the new sentence states, and it is why "links minted through the system-context / `permissive` mint bypass included" is not a flourish — it is the load-bearing consequence: those links have no privileged status at redemption, so they stop serving with everything else. Confirmed on the tree, ⛔ not taken from the report.

### ② Three-dot diff (`git diff origin/main...7be4c2b3b2`, ⛔ never two-dot)

2 files, **+18 / −2**: one TSDoc hunk and one changeset. No schema arm, bound, default, `.describe()` string or behaviour moves.

⭐ The wording choice is right on both counts triage cared about. It takes #16196's landed phrasing rather than inventing a second spelling, and it **points at `enabled` for the whole statement instead of copying the mechanism a third time** — so this fix does not become the next card's N+1 carrier. That is the discipline this card exists to teach, applied to itself.

### ③ Checks, read by name and aggregated by name

31 names on `7be4c2b3b2`: **0 failing**, 16 still running at review time. ⛔ This ACCEPT is not a landing.

### ④ Tier fuse

**136 assistant envelopes, all `claude-opus-5`, zero others** — harness-stamped, ⛔ not the report's self-description.

### ⑤ Pair predicate and governed surface, on the FINAL file list

`--pair 16964` → **exit 0**. `check-governed-merges.mjs --test` → **NOT governed**.

### The changeset — both halves, and ⭐ the dev caught a BROKEN CONTROL in its own measurement

Half 1: `files[]` carries `src/**/*.zod.ts`, and `npm pack --dry-run --json` enumerates `src/data/object.zod.ts` among 2073 entries — the glob checked, not taken on its word. Half 2: the new sentence is verbatim in 22 files under `packages/spec/dist`, with a positive control (22) and a negative control (0).

⭐ **The part worth reading twice**: the neighbour control was first run on the phrase `how the row got there buys it nothing` and returned **0** — and the dev did not accept that zero. The phrase **wraps across a line break** in the source, so a single-line grep could never match it. That is a *broken instrument*, not a reading. Re-run on a non-wrapping phrase it returns 22.

This is the third time this shift that a single-line grep produced a false zero on a wrapped phrase, and the first time the instrument's own author caught it before it entered a conclusion. ⛔ `skip-changeset` would have been wrong here. ⇒ `@objectstack/spec: patch`, correctly owed.

### ⚠️ The declared deviation — force-push on the dev branch

The report self-declares it: an empty routing probe, then a WIP commit, then a squash and a **force-push** to replace it. The standing clause forbids force-push unconditionally.

**Assessment, stated plainly rather than waved through.** The practical blast radius was nil and this seat verified why: no PR existed at the time, and the branch had no other consumer — the rule exists to protect *someone else's* checkout, and there was no someone else. But the rule is unconditional precisely so that nobody has to make that judgement under pressure, and the dev is right that it broke the rule rather than adding on top of the WIP.

⭐ **It reported the breach itself, unprompted, in the field reserved for deviations.** That is the behaviour that keeps an unconditional rule enforceable — a silent force-push is the one this seat could not have found. Recorded, ⛔ not escalated, ⛔ no patch round, and the PR is not held for it. The correct handling next time is one more commit on top; a messy branch history is cheaper than a rewritten one.

### ⭐ The docs-drift row — answered, and it is a NON-finding

The advisory listed `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx` via `ObjectSchemaBase`. This seat said it would check whether that page carries a sibling of the same stale sentence. It does not, and the zero is controlled:

- The page is 561 lines and the instrument fires on it (`object` → 53 hits, `ObjectSchemaBase` → 1).
- Its **only** `ObjectSchemaBase` mention is `:372`, a type-safety bullet: `` `z.input<typeof ObjectSchemaBase>` ``.
- `publicSharing`, `share-link`, `share link` → **zero**. Its only sharing content is `sharingModel: 'private'` in examples — the *principal-based* key the corrected TSDoc explicitly distinguishes from `publicSharing`.

⇒ The row is a true hit on the symbol, not on the sentence. **No sibling carrier, no card.** ⛔ Recorded as a non-finding so nobody re-opens it.

### Handled from the out-of-scope list

- The post-fix sweep for remaining mint-only phrasing across non-test `.ts` (`refuses to create`, `only at mint`, `mint-time check`, `no share links can be issued`) finds **no other carrier** still stating the mint half as complete. ⇒ The N−1 set is now N. Correctly reported as a read rather than a sweep; the broader docblock sweep the dispatch fenced remains a different card.
- #15239 (`sharing.zod.ts`) was fenced off and not inspected — correct, and worth noting that it **landed today in PR #16947**, so it is closed regardless.

### Landing

⛔ Not landed. Enqueue when all 31 names close green. No deviation is claimed on the landing itself.
